# 2026-09-21 — leverage sweep across every project: where Jev can still earn its place

Eric asked for a fresh pass over all projects and conversations to find the
highest-leverage Jev work. Four parallel read-only sweeps (Football, Performance,
Research+Program, Platform + transcripts) were run against the three-condition gate
in `JEV_CAPABILITY_MAP.md`. Nothing was built. This file is the ranking and, for
every candidate, the test that would kill it.

## Read this with the project's record in mind

Every item measured so far moved **down** the map, four in a row. So the ranking
below weights **cheap to kill honestly** as heavily as upside. "Passes gate 3" in a
sweep usually means *the current baseline is visibly weak*, not *someone tried
better code and it still fell short*. Where that is the case it is written
**gate 3 unmeasured**.

## What the sweep overturned

**The map's biggest upside is no longer blocked on a corpus.**
`autoresearch_feature_discovery` (free text becomes model features) was parked
because "there is no input corpus on this box." Two exist:

- `Ath_Medicine/Baylor Medical Diagnostics Report (June 1, 2025 - May 31, 2026).csv`
  — **7,555 notes**, cleaned text in `Note_Expanded`, **3,924** flagged
  `Note_SemanticReady`. Six regex/TF-IDF scripts already read it and feed the
  Senior Staff annual report (`Annual_Report_2025-26_Outline.md`) and the
  534-athlete transfer rollup (`Athlete_Medical_Rollup.csv`).
- `Football/SpringPlayerEvals_SymAnalysis/` — **99 athletes × 4 department
  notes** (position coach, nutrition, strength, academics); the Coach One-Pager
  already prints the trajectory and tier.

So the 09-20 closeout line "**one access conversation unblocks two items**" is half
wrong. `semantic_find` still needs the Kitman/MyLink contracts from Outlook;
text-to-features does not need access at all.

## Ranked

### 1. Ath_Medicine note corpus — surgery tagger first, clinical themes second, CATES grading as the prize

- **Probe (S): surgery status.** `surgery_nlp_extraction.py` `TAG_RULES` (first
  match wins) → `Surgery_NLP_Summary.md` §B. One Choice over the four existing tags
  (completed / planned-discussed / declined / other). 60 notes; **16 of 60 (27%)**
  land in "Review – Other / Ambiguous", and the annual report's "17 previously
  undocumented completed surgeries" headline (§E6) rests on this regex.
- **Next (M): clinical themes** to replace `note_clustering.py` KMeans
  (silhouette **0.165**; six clusters group by provider name, not content). Choice
  over a curated theme list across the 3,924 ready notes.
- **Prize (M, gate 3 unmeasured): CATES A–F pre-grade** from
  `CATES/docs/program/baylor-medical-grading-rubric.md`, decomposed into Nouls
  ("reconstruction game-tested?", "chronic degenerative condition?"), combined in
  code into a suggested grade plus supporting notes for medical staff. There is no
  baseline to beat yet (the rollup only counts notes containing "surger"), and
  portal arrivals have no Baylor notes. Duration rules (">3 weeks concussion")
  stay in code.
- **Kill test (surgery probe):** hand-label the 60. Build on only if Jev agrees
  with the hand label on **≥ 90% of the 44 regex-settled** notes *and* settles
  **≥ 11 of the 16 ambiguous** at Choice top-probability ≥ 0.60 with the label
  correct. Otherwise the regex plus a human read of 16 notes is the answer.
- **Governance question for Eric — not settled by Option C.** These are clinical
  notes with athlete and staff names inside the *text*, not only in a name
  column. Option C cleared "athlete data" on 09-20; whether it extends to
  physician-visit narrative is Eric's call, and names must be stripped from
  `Note_Expanded` itself before anything is sent.
- **Slate:** the annual report is not chartered. Side lane, or it displaces one
  of the five.

### 2. Evidence Library domain tags — the most measurement-ready item on the map

- `SportScienceResearchRepo/evidence-taxonomy.mjs` (`inferTaxonomy`, regex per
  label) → `paper-taxonomy.json` → the Domain filter in
  `football-research-library.jsx` (line ~265).
- 707 records, **407** still `taxonomySource: "rules-v1-unreviewed"`. **300 are
  human-reviewed**, so the labelled eval set already exists.
- Regex baseline on those 300 (measured by the sweep): domain precision **0.63**,
  recall **0.77**, exact domain set in **55 of 300**; "Rehabilitation & Return to
  Sport" wrongly added **133** times.
- **Reuse check, run 2026-09-21:** only **151 of 707** papers (21%) match a title
  already classified in `zotero_classify/out/zotero_topics.csv`, so mapping the
  existing 1,418 labels would cover a fifth at most. This is a new job, not a
  mapping table.
- Shape: one Noul per domain label (multi-label), tier A (published papers).
- **Kill test:** on the 300 reviewed, Jev must reach exact-set match **≥ 150/300**
  and precision **≥ 0.80**, or it does not replace the rules. Caveat to state
  with any result: reviewers may have used full text the rules never saw, so give
  Jev the same fields the rules get.
- **Runner-up in the same repo:** study-design triage for the 1,534 unscreened
  PDFs (`build-pilot-shortlist.mjs` `evidencePriority`; **80 of 197** screened
  records trigger no design pattern). M, since first-page text extraction is the
  state.

### 3. Spring exit-meeting notes → development trajectory

- `Football/SpringPlayerEvals_SymAnalysis/` (`src/semantic_schema.py`,
  `data/semantic_scores.json`, `src/coach_pdf.py`).
- The honest baseline is **not** the Excel keyword rubric (0 on 51% of notes,
  Spearman +0.09). It is the one-off **Claude pass**: ρ = **+0.30** with PFF snaps
  (p = 0.041, **n = 34**), uncalibrated and not reproducible.
- **n = 34 is too small to fit weights** against snaps. Fixed decomposed
  questions with weights set by hand, or report per-question probabilities. Fitting
  would recreate the AUTO_ACCEPT problem.
- **Kill test:** decomposed Jev trajectory must reach ρ ≥ 0.30 on the same 34 and
  give the same answers on a rerun. It cannot *prove* superiority at n = 34
  (the CI is roughly ±0.33); its real value is a scorer you can rerun unchanged on
  next spring's notes. If it lands below 0.30, keep the Claude pass.

### 4. Fireflies meeting → project tag

- 279 transcripts in `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db` (~3/week).
  Consumers exist and none gets a tag today: `meeting-prep` step 2 and
  `status-report` (biweekly, a chartered checkpoint) map meetings to projects by
  hand; `meeting-sync` dumps all meetings into one inbox folder.
- Measured: exact project name appears in **0 of 279**; token matching fires on
  252 but **210** hit more than one project.
- **Gate 3 unmeasured:** the obvious code baseline nobody tried is **attendee →
  project** ("AJ & Coach Red — Camp Load" may settle on its attendee list). Same
  shape as the grep that killed PP_Recruiting entity resolution.
- **Kill test:** build only if an attendee lookup settles **< 80%** of meetings.
- Summaries carry athlete names; the map already gates Fireflies work on
  stripping them. M.

### 5. Tech Inventory athlete-data screening — the only candidate on the slate

- `Tech_Inventory_Analysis/scripts/aliases.py` `ATHLETE_DATA_CATEGORIES`; 188
  products, 75 current candidates, feeding the second-pass form (STATUS next #2).
  Rides the chartered deliverable (Kenny, 10-09; final run 09-29).
- Baseline: category membership flags every "performance" or "video" product and
  clears every comms/admin one.
- **Weakness:** state is a vendor name plus a unit. Without a one-line product
  description as state, Jev is guessing from a brand name. S.
- **Kill test:** hand-check 30 products; Jev must disagree with the category flag
  on ≥ 5 *and* be right on those, or the category rule stays.

### 6. Matchup injury/availability triage — timely, but the hard part is not Jev

- `MatchupAnalysis_FB2026/docs/weekly-routine.md`: the collection script "does not
  pull injury news and never will"; a Monday profile missed the opponent's injury
  report; Keys O1/O3 hinge on one player's status.
- Jev's part is a small Choice (out / doubtful / questionable / day-to-day /
  available / no info) over an article. **The real work is fetching the beat
  coverage**, which is code, and volume is a handful of players a week. M. Worth
  it only as part of a fetch step someone builds anyway.

## Demoted or held

- **`rerank_typesafe`** (map #1 since 09-20): the transcript sweep found **no
  evidence of misses** — all 14 memsearch mentions in 606 human messages over 42
  days are infrastructure failures. A pre-registered measurement is **in progress
  in another session** (`worktree-rerank-typesafe-measure`, commits `bfa5a79`,
  `340df41`); let that result decide. Not re-ranked here to avoid a conflict.
- **Connection-adjudicator pre-filter:** real signal (15 of 24 structural
  candidates rejected; ~13k tokens per 4 pairs), but Mac-only launchd and only two
  runs ever (08-02, 08-09). Confirm it still fires before anything else.
- **memlint dedup as a 3-level Score:** count the warnings and how many are real
  merges first.
- **Flush gate:** low volume (8 flushes in September). **Separately worth fixing:**
  ~282 "transcript missing" skips on the Windows `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV`
  slug look like a path bug in the compiler.
- **BAIR proposal rubric:** textbook composite scoring, four proposals. Volume fails.
- **Coach-doc field-provenance check:** code records which field produced a
  number; Jev would only label claim type. Marginal.

## Near-misses worth recording so they are not re-proposed

- **Women's health survey (slate item):** IRB-approved study (IRB 2373733,
  Proulx). Data is not on disk, and third-party processing is governed by the IRB
  protocol, not Option C.
- **Point of attack from play text:** PFF already carries `rushing.run_position`;
  ESPN text only gives left/middle/right, which a regex reads.
- **Concussion RTP stage from notes:** 92 rows, median 3 words.
- **Kitman injury mechanism:** controlled vocabulary; the Risk engine lacks a field,
  not a judgment.
- **Email triage:** right shape, but morning-briefing was retired 08-14.
- **Tech Inventory survey free text:** hand-coded via 827 lines of `aliases.py` and
  finished for this cycle (1 prose row, 7 unmapped). Revisit next survey cycle.
- **Stop/PreToolUse guards:** "claimed done without verification" is a code check;
  a DexaProject guard would send the content it is guarding.

## Coverage — what was and was not seen

Seen: every folder under `~/Desktop/DEV` on Windows, the Windows Claude Code
transcripts (284 files, 606 human messages, last 42 days), the compiled knowledge
index and global memory. **Not seen:** Mac raw transcripts, the SecondBrain vault
(Mac-only), the fresh `pff.db` (Windows copy is from June 1), CFBD `playText` (not
on this box), Baylor Outlook. A Mac-side pass could add candidates; it is unlikely
to remove any above.

## Next actions

1. **Eric decides the Ath_Medicine governance question** (does Option C cover
   clinical note text?). Everything in #1 waits on it.
2. **Evidence Library kill test** (#2) needs no decision and no new data: run Jev
   over the 300 reviewed records with the rule's own fields. Tier A, pennies.
3. **Attendee-lookup baseline for Fireflies** (#4): pure code, settles whether a
   Jev build is needed.
4. Let the in-flight rerank measurement land before touching the map's #1.

Every item measured so far moved **down** the map, four in a row. So the ranking
below weights **cheap to kill honestly** as heavily as upside. "Passes gate 3" in a
sweep usually means *the current baseline is visibly weak*, not *someone tried
better code and it still fell short*. Where that is the case it is written
**gate 3 unmeasured**.

`autoresearch_feature_discovery` (free text becomes model features) was parked
because "there is no input corpus on this box." Two exist:

  notes** (position coach, nutrition, strength, academics); the Coach One-Pager

  undocumented completed surgeries" headline (§E6) rests on this regex.

I swept every project under DEV plus about six weeks of your Windows conversation history, looking for work where Jev beats plain code. It's written up as draft PR #18 in TypeSafe_Sandbox; nothing was built or run against the API. Coverage caveat: I couldn't reach the Mac transcripts, your notes vault, the up-to-date `pff.db` or Outlook.

**The main finding:** your capability map says its biggest upside, turning free text into model features, is blocked because no text exists on this machine. That's wrong. Two sets exist and something already reads each:
- **`Ath_Medicine`:** 7,555 medical diagnostics notes. Six regex/TF-IDF scripts already read them to feed the Senior Staff annual report and the transfer-portal medical rollup.
- **`Football/SpringPlayerEvals_SymAnalysis`:** 99 athletes × 4 department notes, feeding the Coach One-Pager.

**Ranked.** Each has a pass/fail test decided in advance, because every idea measured so far has dropped down the list:
1. **Ath_Medicine notes.** Start with the surgery tagger: 27% of surgery mentions come out "ambiguous", and the annual report's "17 previously undocumented surgeries" figure rests on it. Next, replace the note clustering, which groups notes by provider name instead of clinical content. The big prize is pre-grading athletes on the CATES A–F medical scale, but nothing exists to compare it against yet.
2. **Evidence Library domain tags** (SportScienceResearchRepo). This is the only one testable today, with no decision or new data needed: 300 papers are already human-reviewed. The current rules get the full domain set right on only 55 of 300. I checked: only 151 of the 707 papers overlap Jev's existing Zotero labels, so this is new work, not a reuse.
3. **Spring exit notes → development trajectory.** The bar is the one-off Claude pass (ρ 0.30 with snaps), not the weak keyword rubric. With 34 players there's too little data to fit weights. The real value is a scorer you can rerun unchanged next spring.
4. **Fireflies meeting → project tag.** 279 meetings, and meeting-prep and the status report both need the tag. Project names match 0 of 279. Nobody has tried matching on who attended, and that might settle most meetings without Jev.
5. **Tech Inventory athlete-data screening.** The only candidate tied to your Fall slate (Kenny, 10-09). Jev would only see a vendor name, which is thin.
6. **Matchup injury triage.** Timely, but fetching the news articles is the real work.

**Held back:**
- **Memsearch reranking** (your map's current #1): I found no sign in your conversations that search misses answers. Another session is already running its test; I left it to that result.
- **Women's health survey:** the data isn't on disk yet, and the IRB protocol governs sending it anywhere, not your Option C clearance.
- **Unrelated bug:** the memory compiler skipped about 282 Windows sessions as "transcript missing". That looks like a path bug worth fixing on its own.

**Decision for you:** does your Option C clearance extend to clinical note text? These notes have athlete and staff names inside the text itself, so the names would need stripping first. Everything in #1 waits on your answer. #2 is ready to run today whenever you want it.

Sanity check: I re-read your ask against the write-up and confirmed the commit is pushed and the PR is open. The PR is docs only.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal bounded client for the TypeSafe System One endpoint. Stdlib only.

Lifted from the skill router's `ask()`, which is the only HTTP path in this repo that
has been reviewed. The important property is the same here even though a batch job is
not latency-critical: **the timeout is real wall-clock time, not a socket timeout.**

`urlopen(timeout=)` bounds each individual blocking operation, so DNS, connect, TLS
and every body read each get the full value; a server trickling bytes never trips it.
The request therefore runs on a daemon thread and is abandoned if it overruns. In a
batch of 1,400 that is the difference between one slow record and a job that never
finishes.

NOTE: `skill_router/router.py` on branch `worktree-jev-skill-router` still carries its
own copy of this logic. When that branch merges, point it at this module so there is
one HTTP path rather than two that can drift.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import threading
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ENDPOINT = os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_ENDPOINT", "https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone")
MODEL = os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_MODEL", "jev-latest")
MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024


class JevError(RuntimeError):
    """Anything that stopped us getting a usable answer."""


def api_key() -> str:
    """Env var first, then ~/.claude/typesafe.env.

    The key must keep its `apikey_` prefix. A 401 means the key value is wrong; a 422
    means the request body is. That split is the fastest way to tell which end is at
    fault, and it has cost this project time before.
    """
    key = os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_API_KEY")
    if key and key.strip():
        return key.strip()
    env_file = Path(os.path.expanduser("~")) / ".claude" / "typesafe.env"
    try:
        for line in env_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            name, _, value = line.strip().partition("=")
            if name.strip() == "TYPESAFE_API_KEY" and value.strip():
                return value.strip().strip("\"'")
    except OSError:
        pass
    raise JevError(
        "no TYPESAFE_API_KEY in the environment or ~/.claude/typesafe.env"
    )


def system_one(state, questions: dict, key: str, timeout: float = 20.0) -> dict:
    """POST one request and return its `answers` map. Raises JevError on anything else.

    No retries here on purpose: the caller owns retry policy, because what is safe to
    retry in a resumable batch job is not what is safe in a hook.
    """
    body = json.dumps(
        {"state": state, "model": MODEL, "questions": questions}
    ).encode("utf-8")
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        ENDPOINT,
        data=body,
        headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {key}",
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
        method="POST",
    )

    outcome: dict = {}

    def perform() -> None:
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
                raw = response.read(MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES)
            outcome["data"] = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
        except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - handed back to the caller
            outcome["error"] = error

    worker = threading.Thread(target=perform, daemon=True)
    worker.start()
    worker.join(timeout)
    if worker.is_alive():
        raise JevError(f"wall-clock timeout after {timeout}s")
    if "error" in outcome:
        raise JevError(f"{type(outcome['error']).__name__}: {outcome['error']}")

    payload = outcome.get("data")
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise JevError("response is not an object")
    answers = payload.get("answers")
    if not isinstance(answers, dict) or not answers:
        raise JevError("response carried no answers")
    return answers
# zotero_classify

Gives every research record in the Zotero library a topic, using TypeSafe's Jev. When
it is not confident enough to name one, it reports the broader domain instead, so
every record still gets a true label. Implements the `classification_using_confidence`
cookbook against a taxonomy drafted for this library.

Tier A: published literature and metadata only. No athlete data leaves the machine.

```bash
python taxonomy.py                 # print and sanity-check the taxonomy
python library.py                  # what the bridge index holds (read-only)
python validate.py --collect       # 41 hand-labelled records, ~41 calls
python validate.py                 # sweep the cutoff over saved answers, no calls
python classify.py --limit 20 --out runs/sample.jsonl   # try it small (new file)
python classify.py --out runs/full.jsonl                # all 1,418, ~86s, ~$0.07
python classify.py --out runs/full.jsonl --report       # re-read a run, no calls
python export.py                   # out/zotero_topics.csv + out/LIBRARY_MAP.md
```

Runs append to JSONL and skip records already done, so an interrupted run resumes and
a crash never costs the calls already paid for.

Needs `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in the environment or in `~/.claude/typesafe.env`, keeping
its `apikey_` prefix. Needs the zotero-research bridge's `library.db`; override its
location with `ZOTERO_BRIDGE_DB`.

Design, measurements, the cutoff argument and the taxonomy mistake the first run
exposed: `../docs/ZOTERO_CLASSIFICATION.md`.

# Evidence Library domain tags — does Jev beat the regex?

Item #2 of the 2026-09-21 leverage sweep. Eric said go on 2026-09-21.

## Pre-registration (written and committed before any API call)

**Question.** `SportScienceResearchRepo/evidence-taxonomy.mjs` tags each paper with
1–3 of 8 domains by counting regex hits. 407 of 707 published papers still carry
those rule tags unreviewed. Does one Jev Noul per domain, over the *same fields the
rules read*, recover the reviewed domains better enough to replace the rules?

**Labels.** The 300 records in `paper-taxonomy.json` whose `taxonomySource` is
`full-text-screening` (197) or `zotero-paper-brief` (103). Provenance is **not
recorded in the repo**: batches of 12 screened in a day, alongside dozens of
`docs/batch_rN_aM.json` files, suggest agent-run full-text review rather than Eric
hand-labelling. So this measures **agreement with full-text reviewed labels**, not
proven human truth. Reviewers saw full text; both the rules and Jev see only the
`papers.json` fields below, so neither has an advantage over the other.

**State per paper.** `citation, abstract, methods, findings, tldr,
practicalImplications, athleteDev, rtp` — the union `inferTaxonomy` reads for
domains. Median ~2,000 characters.

**Questions.** 8 Nouls, one per domain, definitions in `evidence_tags/domains.py`,
written from the taxonomy names before seeing any Jev output. At most **one**
revision of the definitions is allowed after the first run, and if it happens both
results are reported.

**Decision rule.** Same shape as the rules: take every domain with P ≥ t, capped at
the top 3, and at least the top 1. The threshold t is chosen on the **tune half**
(even paper ids) and reported on the **test half** (odd ids). The tune-half number is
not the result.

**Kill test (from the sweep handoff).** On the test half, Jev must reach:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Evidence Library domain tags: Jev vs the regex rules, on the 300 reviewed records.

    python measure.py --collect     # ~300 calls, appends runs/reviewed.jsonl, resumable
    python measure.py               # score saved answers against rules and labels, no calls

Pre-registration and results: ../docs/EVIDENCE_TAGS.md. Tier A: published papers only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent / "zotero_classify"))
import jev_client  # noqa: E402

from domains import DOMAINS, questions  # noqa: E402

RUN = HERE / "runs" / "reviewed.jsonl"
FIELDS = ("citation", "abstract", "methods", "findings", "tldr",
          "practicalImplications", "athleteDev", "rtp")
REVIEWED = {"full-text-screening", "zotero-paper-brief"}
NAMES = list(DOMAINS)

# Kill test, pre-registered in docs/EVIDENCE_TAGS.md.
KILL_EXACT = 0.50
KILL_PRECISION = 0.80


def repo() -> Path:
    env = os.environ.get("EVIDENCE_REPO")
    candidates = [Path(env)] if env else []
    home = Path(os.path.expanduser("~"))
    candidates += [home / "Desktop" / "DEV" / "SportScienceResearchRepo",
                   home / "DEV" / "SportScienceResearchRepo"]
    for path in candidates:
        if (path / "papers.json").exists():
            return path
    raise SystemExit("SportScienceResearchRepo not found; set EVIDENCE_REPO")


def load() -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    root = repo()
    papers = {str(p["id"]): p for p in json.loads((root / "papers.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))}
    taxonomy = json.loads((root / "paper-taxonomy.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["records"]
    labels = {r["id"]: set(r["domains"]) for r in taxonomy if r["taxonomySource"] in REVIEWED}
    return papers, labels


def state_for(paper: dict) -> dict:
    return {k: paper[k] for k in FIELDS if paper.get(k)}


def collect() -> None:
    papers, labels = load()
    RUN.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    done = set()
    if RUN.exists():
        done = {json.loads(line)["id"] for line in RUN.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()}
    key = jev_client.api_key()
    todo = [i for i in sorted(labels, key=int) if i not in done]
    print(f"{len(done)} saved, {len(todo)} to collect")
    failures = 0
    with RUN.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as out:
        for n, pid in enumerate(todo, 1):
            started = time.monotonic()
            try:
                answers = jev_client.system_one(state_for(papers[pid]), questions(), key, timeout=20.0)
            except jev_client.JevError as error:
                failures += 1
                print(f"  {pid}: {error}")
                if failures >= 5:
                    raise SystemExit("5 failures, stopping; rerun to resume")
                continue
            nouls = {q.removeprefix("domain::"): a.get("noul") for q, a in answers.items()}
            if any(not isinstance(nouls.get(name), (int, float)) for name in NAMES):
                failures += 1
                print(f"  {pid}: incomplete answers, not saved")
                continue
            out.write(json.dumps({"id": pid, "nouls": nouls,
                                  "ms": round((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)}) + "\n")
            out.flush()
            if n % 50 == 0:
                print(f"  {n}/{len(todo)}")
    print("done")


def rules_domains() -> dict:
    result = subprocess.run(["node", str(HERE / "rules_dump.mjs"), str(repo())],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", check=True)
    return {k: set(v) for k, v in json.loads(result.stdout).items()}


def decide(nouls: dict, t: float) -> set:
    ranked = sorted(NAMES, key=lambda name: -nouls[name])
    chosen = [name for name in ranked[:3] if nouls[name] >= t]
    return set(chosen or ranked[:1])


def score(pred: dict, labels: dict, ids: list) -> dict:
    tp = fp = fn = exact = 0
    for i in ids:
        p, g = pred[i], labels[i]
        tp += len(p & g)
        fp += len(p - g)
        fn += len(g - p)
        exact += p == g
    precision = tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else 0.0
    recall = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else 0.0
    return {"n": len(ids), "exact": exact, "exact_rate": exact / len(ids),
            "precision": precision, "recall": recall,
            "f1": 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall) if precision + recall else 0.0}


def per_domain(pred: dict, labels: dict, ids: list) -> list:
    rows = []
    for name in NAMES:
        tp = sum(name in pred[i] and name in labels[i] for i in ids)
        fp = sum(name in pred[i] and name not in labels[i] for i in ids)
        fn = sum(name not in pred[i] and name in labels[i] for i in ids)
        rows.append((name, tp, fp, fn))
    return rows


def fmt(s: dict) -> str:
    return (f"exact {s['exact']}/{s['n']} ({s['exact_rate']:.0%})  "
            f"P {s['precision']:.2f}  R {s['recall']:.2f}  F1 {s['f1']:.2f}")


def report() -> None:
    _, labels = load()
    saved = {}
    for line in RUN.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.strip():
            row = json.loads(line)
            saved[row["id"]] = row["nouls"]
    ids = [i for i in sorted(labels, key=int) if i in saved]
    missing = len(labels) - len(ids)
    tune = [i for i in ids if int(i) % 2 == 0]
    test = [i for i in ids if int(i) % 2 == 1]
    rules = rules_domains()

    print(f"records: {len(ids)} scored, {missing} missing; tune {len(tune)}, test {len(test)}\n")
    print("rules, all   :", fmt(score(rules, labels, ids)))
    print("rules, tune  :", fmt(score(rules, labels, tune)))
    print("rules, test  :", fmt(score(rules, labels, test)))

    print("\nthreshold sweep on TUNE half (choose by exact rate, then F1):")
    best = None
    for t in [x / 100 for x in range(10, 96, 5)]:
        s = score({i: decide(saved[i], t) for i in tune}, labels, tune)
        print(f"  t={t:.2f}  {fmt(s)}")
        k = (s["exact_rate"], s["f1"])
        if best is None or k > best[0]:
            best = (k, t)
    t = best[1]
    jev_test = {i: decide(saved[i], t) for i in test}
    s_test = score(jev_test, labels, test)
    s_rules = score(rules, labels, test)
    print(f"\nchosen t = {t:.2f} (tune half)")
    print("JEV,  test   :", fmt(s_test))
    print("rules, test  :", fmt(s_rules))

    passed = (s_test["exact_rate"] >= KILL_EXACT and s_test["precision"] >= KILL_PRECISION
              and s_test["exact_rate"] > s_rules["exact_rate"]
              and s_test["precision"] > s_rules["precision"])
    print(f"\nKILL TEST (exact >= {KILL_EXACT:.0%}, precision >= {KILL_PRECISION}, beats rules on both): "
          f"{'PASS' if passed else 'FAIL'}")

    print("\nper-domain on test half (tp / fp / fn):   JEV   |   rules")
    jr = per_domain(jev_test, labels, test)
    rr = per_domain(rules, labels, test)
    for (name, a, b, c), (_, d, e, f) in zip(jr, rr):
        print(f"  {name:34s} {a:3d}/{b:3d}/{c:3d}   |  {d:3d}/{e:3d}/{f:3d}")

    ms = sorted(json.loads(line)["ms"] for line in RUN.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip())
    print(f"\nlatency median {ms[len(ms)//2]} ms")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--collect", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    collect() if args.collect else report()

"""Evidence Library domain tags: Jev vs the regex rules, on the 300 reviewed records.

    python measure.py --collect     # ~300 calls, appends runs/reviewed.jsonl, resumable
    python measure.py               # score saved answers against rules and labels, no calls

Pre-registration and results: ../docs/EVIDENCE_TAGS.md. Tier A: published papers only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent / "zotero_classify"))
import jev_client  # noqa: E402

from domains import DOMAINS, questions  # noqa: E402

RUN = HERE / "runs" / "reviewed.jsonl"
FIELDS = ("citation", "abstract", "methods", "findings", "tldr",
          "practicalImplications", "athleteDev", "rtp")
REVIEWED = {"full-text-screening", "zotero-paper-brief"}
NAMES = list(DOMAINS)

# Kill test, pre-registered in docs/EVIDENCE_TAGS.md.
KILL_EXACT = 0.50
KILL_PRECISION = 0.80


def repo() -> Path:
    env = os.environ.get("EVIDENCE_REPO")
    candidates = [Path(env)] if env else []
    home = Path(os.path.expanduser("~"))
    candidates += [home / "Desktop" / "DEV" / "SportScienceResearchRepo",
                   home / "DEV" / "SportScienceResearchRepo"]
    for path in candidates:
        if (path / "papers.json").exists():
            return path
    raise SystemExit("SportScienceResearchRepo not found; set EVIDENCE_REPO")


def load() -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    root = repo()
    papers = {str(p["id"]): p for p in json.loads((root / "papers.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))}
    taxonomy = json.loads((root / "paper-taxonomy.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["records"]
    labels = {r["id"]: set(r["domains"]) for r in taxonomy if r["taxonomySource"] in REVIEWED}
    return papers, labels


def state_for(paper: dict) -> dict:
    return {k: paper[k] for k in FIELDS if paper.get(k)}


def collect() -> None:
    papers, labels = load()
    RUN.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    done = set()
    if RUN.exists():
        done = {json.loads(line)["id"] for line in RUN.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()}
    key = jev_client.api_key()
    todo = [i for i in sorted(labels, key=int) if i not in done]
    print(f"{len(done)} saved, {len(todo)} to collect")
    failures = 0
    with RUN.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as out:
        for n, pid in enumerate(todo, 1):
            started = time.monotonic()
            try:
                answers = jev_client.system_one(state_for(papers[pid]), questions(), key, timeout=20.0)
            except jev_client.JevError as error:
                failures += 1
                print(f"  {pid}: {error}")
                if failures >= 5:
                    raise SystemExit("5 failures, stopping; rerun to resume")
                continue
            nouls = {q.removeprefix("domain::"): a.get("noul") for q, a in answers.items()}
            if any(not isinstance(nouls.get(name), (int, float)) for name in NAMES):
                failures += 1
                print(f"  {pid}: incomplete answers, not saved")
                continue
            out.write(json.dumps({"id": pid, "nouls": nouls,
                                  "ms": round((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)}) + "\n")
            out.flush()
            if n % 50 == 0:
                print(f"  {n}/{len(todo)}")
    print("done")


def rules_domains() -> dict:
    result = subprocess.run(["node", str(HERE / "rules_dump.mjs"), str(repo())],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", check=True)
    return {k: set(v) for k, v in json.loads(result.stdout).items()}


def decide(nouls: dict, t: float) -> set:
    ranked = sorted(NAMES, key=lambda name: -nouls[name])
    chosen = [name for name in ranked[:3] if nouls[name] >= t]
    return set(chosen or ranked[:1])


def score(pred: dict, labels: dict, ids: list) -> dict:
    tp = fp = fn = exact = 0

        p, g = pred[i], labels[i]

        fn += len(g - p)

    recall = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else 0.0

            "precision": precision, "recall": recall,
            "f1": 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall) if precision + recall else 0.0}

    return rows

    return (f"exact {s['exact']}/{s['n']} ({s['exact_rate']:.0%})  "
            f"P {s['precision']:.2f}  R {s['recall']:.2f}  F1 {s['f1']:.2f}")


def report() -> None:
    _, labels = load()
    saved = {}
    for line in RUN.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.strip():
            row = json.loads(line)
            saved[row["id"]] = row["nouls"]
    ids = [i for i in sorted(labels, key=int) if i in saved]
    missing = len(labels) - len(ids)
    tune = [i for i in ids if int(i) % 2 == 0]
    test = [i for i in ids if int(i) % 2 == 1]
    rules = rules_domains()

    print(f"records: {len(ids)} scored, {missing} missing; tune {len(tune)}, test {len(test)}\n")
    print("rules, all   :", fmt(score(rules, labels, ids)))
    print("rules, tune  :", fmt(score(rules, labels, tune)))
    print("rules, test  :", fmt(score(rules, labels, test)))

    print("\nthreshold sweep on TUNE half (choose by exact rate, then F1):")
    best = None
    for t in [x / 100 for x in range(10, 96, 5)]:
        s = score({i: decide(saved[i], t) for i in tune}, labels, tune)
        print(f"  t={t:.2f}  {fmt(s)}")
        k = (s["exact_rate"], s["f1"])
        if best is None or k > best[0]:
            best = (k, t)
    t = best[1]
    jev_test = {i: decide(saved[i], t) for i in test}
    s_test = score(jev_test, labels, test)
    s_rules = score(rules, labels, test)
    print(f"\nchosen t = {t:.2f} (tune half)")
    print("JEV,  test   :", fmt(s_test))
    print("rules, test  :", fmt(s_rules))

    passed = (s_test["exact_rate"] >= KILL_EXACT and s_test["precision"] >= KILL_PRECISION
              and s_test["exact_rate"] > s_rules["exact_rate"]
              and s_test["precision"] > s_rules["precision"])
    print(f"\nKILL TEST (exact >= {KILL_EXACT:.0%}, precision >= {KILL_PRECISION}, beats rules on both): "
          f"{'PASS' if passed else 'FAIL'}")

    print("\nper-domain on test half (tp / fp / fn):   JEV   |   rules")
    jr = per_domain(jev_test, labels, test)
    rr = per_domain(rules, labels, test)
    for (name, a, b, c), (_, d, e, f) in zip(jr, rr):
        print(f"  {name:34s} {a:3d}/{b:3d}/{c:3d}   |  {d:3d}/{e:3d}/{f:3d}")

    ms = sorted(json.loads(line)["ms"] for line in RUN.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip())
    print(f"\nlatency median {ms[len(ms)//2]} ms")

# Evidence Library domain tags — does Jev beat the regex?

Item #2 of the 2026-09-21 leverage sweep. Eric said go on 2026-09-21.

## Pre-registration (written and committed before any API call)

**Question.** `SportScienceResearchRepo/evidence-taxonomy.mjs` tags each paper with
1–3 of 8 domains by counting regex hits. 407 of 707 published papers still carry
those rule tags unreviewed. Does one Jev Noul per domain, over the *same fields the
rules read*, recover the reviewed domains better enough to replace the rules?

**Labels.** The 300 records in `paper-taxonomy.json` whose `taxonomySource` is
`full-text-screening` (197) or `zotero-paper-brief` (103). Provenance is **not
recorded in the repo**: batches of 12 screened in a day, alongside dozens of
`docs/batch_rN_aM.json` files, suggest agent-run full-text review rather than Eric
hand-labelling. So this measures **agreement with full-text reviewed labels**, not
proven human truth. Reviewers saw full text; both the rules and Jev see only the
`papers.json` fields below, so neither has an advantage over the other.

**State per paper.** `citation, abstract, methods, findings, tldr,
practicalImplications, athleteDev, rtp` — the union `inferTaxonomy` reads for
domains. Median ~2,000 characters.

**Questions.** 8 Nouls, one per domain, definitions in `evidence_tags/domains.py`,
written from the taxonomy names before seeing any Jev output. At most **one**
revision of the definitions is allowed after the first run, and if it happens both
results are reported.

**Decision rule.** Same shape as the rules: take every domain with P ≥ t, capped at
the top 3, and at least the top 1. The threshold t is chosen on the **tune half**
(even paper ids) and reported on the **test half** (odd ids). The tune-half number is
not the result.

**Kill test (from the sweep handoff).** On the test half, Jev must reach:

- **exact domain-set match ≥ 50% of records**, and
- **micro precision ≥ 0.80**,

and beat the rules on both. Miss either and the rules stay. The rules' baseline, as
measured by the sweep over all 300: exact set 55/300 (18%), precision 0.63, recall
0.77. It is re-measured here on the same halves by running the real `.mjs`.

**Cost ceiling.** 300 requests × ~1k tokens ≈ $0.02. Tier A: published papers only.

## Result

_Not run yet._

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a blind 20-paper preference sheet: Jev's domain tags vs the rules', unlabelled.

    python blind_check.py           # writes blind_check.md (for Eric) + runs/blind_key.json
    python blind_check.py --score   # reads Eric's A/B picks from blind_check.md, reports

Only test-half papers where the two tag sets differ. Which side is A is randomised per
paper with a fixed seed; the key never appears in the sheet. No API calls.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import random
import re
from pathlib import Path

import measure

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SHEET = HERE / "blind_check.md"
KEY = HERE / "runs" / "blind_key.json"
T = 0.15  # chosen on the tune half in the first run
N = 20
SEED = 20260921


def build() -> None:
    papers, labels = measure.load()
    saved = {}
    for line in measure.RUN.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.strip():
            row = json.loads(line)
            saved[row["id"]] = row["nouls"]
    rules = measure.rules_domains()
    pool = [i for i in sorted(saved, key=int)
            if int(i) % 2 == 1 and measure.decide(saved[i], T) != rules[i]]
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    picks = rng.sample(pool, min(N, len(pool)))
    key, lines = {}, [
        "# Blind check: which domain tags fit the paper better?",
        "",
        "For each paper, read the summary and put **A**, **B** or **=** (no preference)",
        "after `Pick:`. The two sets come from two different taggers; which is which is",
        "hidden and shuffled per paper. Then run `python blind_check.py --score`.",
        "",
        f"{len(picks)} papers, drawn from the {len(pool)} held-out papers where the taggers disagree.",
        "",
    ]
    for n, pid in enumerate(picks, 1):
        jev, rule = sorted(measure.decide(saved[pid], T)), sorted(rules[pid])
        jev_is_a = rng.random() < 0.5
        a, b = (jev, rule) if jev_is_a else (rule, jev)
        key[pid] = {"A": "jev" if jev_is_a else "rules", "reviewed": sorted(labels[pid])}
        paper = papers[pid]
        summary = (paper.get("tldr") or paper.get("abstract") or "").strip().replace("\n", " ")
        lines += [
            f"## {n}. paper {pid}",
            "",
            f"**{paper.get('citation', '').strip()}**",
            "",
            f"> {summary[:700]}{'…' if len(summary) > 700 else ''}",
            "",
            f"- **A:** {', '.join(a)}",
            f"- **B:** {', '.join(b)}",
            "",
            "Pick: ",
            "",
        ]
    SHEET.write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
    KEY.write_text(json.dumps(key, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {SHEET.name} ({len(picks)} papers from a pool of {len(pool)}) and {KEY.name}")


def score() -> None:
    key = json.loads(KEY.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    text = SHEET.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    blocks = re.findall(r"## \d+\. paper (\d+).*?Pick:[ \t]*([AB=]?)", text, flags=re.S)
    tally = {"jev": 0, "rules": 0, "tie": 0, "blank": 0}
    for pid, pick in blocks:
        if not pick:
            tally["blank"] += 1
        elif pick == "=":
            tally["tie"] += 1
        else:
            winner = key[pid]["A"] if pick == "A" else ("rules" if key[pid]["A"] == "jev" else "jev")
            tally[winner] += 1
    print(tally)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--score", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    score() if args.score else build()

# Evidence Library domain tags — does Jev beat the regex?

Item #2 of the 2026-09-21 leverage sweep. Eric said go on 2026-09-21.

## Pre-registration (written and committed before any API call)

**Question.** `SportScienceResearchRepo/evidence-taxonomy.mjs` tags each paper with
1–3 of 8 domains by counting regex hits. 407 of 707 published papers still carry
those rule tags unreviewed. Does one Jev Noul per domain, over the *same fields the
rules read*, recover the reviewed domains better enough to replace the rules?

**Labels.** The 300 records in `paper-taxonomy.json` whose `taxonomySource` is
`full-text-screening` (197) or `zotero-paper-brief` (103). Provenance is **not
recorded in the repo**: batches of 12 screened in a day, alongside dozens of
`docs/batch_rN_aM.json` files, suggest agent-run full-text review rather than Eric
hand-labelling. So this measures **agreement with full-text reviewed labels**, not
proven human truth. Reviewers saw full text; both the rules and Jev see only the
`papers.json` fields below, so neither has an advantage over the other.

**State per paper.** `citation, abstract, methods, findings, tldr,
practicalImplications, athleteDev, rtp` — the union `inferTaxonomy` reads for
domains. Median ~2,000 characters.

**Questions.** 8 Nouls, one per domain, definitions in `evidence_tags/domains.py`,
written from the taxonomy names before seeing any Jev output. At most **one**
revision of the definitions is allowed after the first run, and if it happens both
results are reported.

**Decision rule.** Same shape as the rules: take every domain with P ≥ t, capped at
the top 3, and at least the top 1. The threshold t is chosen on the **tune half**
(even paper ids) and reported on the **test half** (odd ids). The tune-half number is
not the result.

**Kill test (from the sweep handoff).** On the test half, Jev must reach:

- **exact domain-set match ≥ 50% of records**, and
- **micro precision ≥ 0.80**,

and beat the rules on both. Miss either and the rules stay. The rules' baseline, as

content.text:
I ran the Evidence Library test. **It failed the pass bar I set before running it, even though Jev beat the regex rules on every measure.** #1 stays as written, per your call.

The test: Jev tagged the 300 reviewed papers with the same fields the regex rules read, and both were scored against the reviewers' labels. I committed the pass/fail bar before making any call, chose Jev's cutoff on half the papers, and scored on the other 151:

| held-out 151 papers | exact domain set | precision | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| current rules | 17% | 0.63 | 0.69 |
| Jev | **43%** (bar was 50%) | **0.85** | **0.82** |

- **It misses the bar on exact matches only.** Precision cleared 0.80. I haven't lowered the bar after seeing the result.
- **The rules' worst habit goes away.** Wrong "Rehabilitation & Return to Sport" tags drop from 68 to 1, and false tags overall from 161 to 52.
- **The gap is mostly about how many tags, not which ones.** The best cutoff turned out to be 0.15, so Jev reads "main subject" more strictly than the reviewers, who tag about 3 domains per paper.
- **The labels may not be a human standard.** No record says who reviewed these papers, and the batch pattern looks like agent review. The 50% bar was my own guess, not based on how often reviewers agree.

The run cost about $0.02 for 300 calls, with no failures. Re-running the scorer from the saved answers needs no API calls.

**Your part, about 15 minutes:** Jev and the rules disagree on 135 of the 151 held-out papers. I put 20 of them in `TypeSafe_Sandbox/evidence_tags/blind_check.md` (on the PR branch). Each paper shows its summary and two unlabelled tag sets, with the order shuffled. Mark each A, B or = without opening `runs/blind_key.json`, then run:

```
python evidence_tags/blind_check.py --score
```

If Jev wins at least 70% of the papers where you had a preference, I replace the rule tags on the 407 unreviewed papers, marked as Jev tags so they stay separate from reviewed ones. Below that, the rules stay and this item closes.

Everything is committed and pushed to branch `leverage-sweep-0921`; draft PR #18 now includes this result, and `STATUS.md` and the handoff are updated.

# Evidence Library domain tags — does Jev beat the regex?

Item #2 of the 2026-09-21 leverage sweep. Eric said go on 2026-09-21.

## Pre-registration (written and committed before any API call)

**Question.** `SportScienceResearchRepo/evidence-taxonomy.mjs` tags each paper with
1–3 of 8 domains by counting regex hits. 407 of 707 published papers still carry
those rule tags unreviewed. Does one Jev Noul per domain, over the *same fields the
rules read*, recover the reviewed domains better enough to replace the rules?

**Labels.** The 300 records in `paper-taxonomy.json` whose `taxonomySource` is
`full-text-screening` (197) or `zotero-paper-brief` (103). Provenance is **not

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a blind 20-paper preference sheet: Jev's domain tags vs the rules', unlabelled.

    python blind_check.py           # writes blind_check.md (for Eric) + runs/blind_key.json
    python blind_check.py --score   # reads Eric's A/B picks from blind_check.md, reports

Only test-half papers where the two tag sets differ. Which side is A is randomised per
paper with a fixed seed; the key never appears in the sheet. No API calls.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import random
import re
from pathlib import Path

import measure

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SHEET = HERE / "blind_check.md"
KEY = HERE / "runs" / "blind_key.json"
T = 0.15  # chosen on the tune half in the first run
N = 20
SEED = 20260921


def build() -> None:
    papers, labels = measure.load()
    saved = {}
    for line in measure.RUN.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.strip():
            row = json.loads(line)
            saved[row["id"]] = row["nouls"]
    rules = measure.rules_domains()
    pool = [i for i in sorted(saved, key=int)
            if int(i) % 2 == 1 and measure.decide(saved[i], T) != rules[i]]
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    picks = rng.sample(pool, min(N, len(pool)))
    key, lines = {}, [
        "# Blind check: which domain tags fit the paper better?",
        "",
        "For each paper, read the summary and put **A**, **B** or **=** (no preference)",
        "after `Pick:`. The two sets come from two different taggers; which is which is",
        "hidden and shuffled per paper. Then run `python blind_check.py --score`.",
        "",
        f"{len(picks)} papers, drawn from the {len(pool)} held-out papers where the taggers disagree.",
        "",
    ]
    for n, pid in enumerate(picks, 1):
        jev, rule = sorted(measure.decide(saved[pid], T)), sorted(rules[pid])
        jev_is_a = rng.random() < 0.5

1	# Evidence Library domain tags — does Jev beat the regex?
2	
3	Item #2 of the 2026-09-21 leverage sweep. Eric said go on 2026-09-21.
4	
5	## Pre-registration (written and committed before any API call)
6	
7	**Question.** `SportScienceResearchRepo/evidence-taxonomy.mjs` tags each paper with
8	1–3 of 8 domains by counting regex hits. 407 of 707 published papers still carry
9	those rule tags unreviewed. Does one Jev Noul per domain, over the *same fields the
10	rules read*, recover the reviewed domains better enough to replace the rules?
11	
12	**Labels.** The 300 records in `paper-taxonomy.json` whose `taxonomySource` is
13	`full-text-screening` (197) or `zotero-paper-brief` (103). Provenance is **not
14	recorded in the repo**: batches of 12 screened in a day, alongside dozens of
15	`docs/batch_rN_aM.json` files, suggest agent-run full-text review rather than Eric
16	hand-labelling. So this measures **agreement with full-text reviewed labels**, not
17	proven human truth. Reviewers saw full text; both the rules and Jev see only the
18	`papers.json` fields below, so neither has an advantage over the other.
19	
20	**State per paper.** `citation, abstract, methods, findings, tldr,
21	practicalImplications, athleteDev, rtp` — the union `inferTaxonomy` reads for
22	domains. Median ~2,000 characters.
23	
24	**Questions.** 8 Nouls, one per domain, definitions in `evidence_tags/domains.py`,
25	written from the taxonomy names before seeing any Jev output. At most **one**
26	revision of the definitions is allowed after the first run, and if it happens both
27	results are reported.
28	
29	**Decision rule.** Same shape as the rules: take every domain with P ≥ t, capped at
30	the top 3, and at least the top 1. The threshold t is chosen on the **tune half**
31	(even paper ids) and reported on the **test half** (odd ids). The tune-half number is
32	not the result.
33	
34	**Kill test (from the sweep handoff).** On the test half, Jev must reach:
35	
36	- **exact domain-set match ≥ 50% of records**, and
37	- **micro precision ≥ 0.80**,
38	
39	and beat the rules on both. Miss either and the rules stay. The rules' baseline, as
40	measured by the sweep over all 300: exact set 55/300 (18%), precision 0.63, recall
41	0.77. It is re-measured here on the same halves by running the real `.mjs`.
42	
43	**Cost ceiling.** 300 requests × ~1k tokens ≈ $0.02. Tier A: published papers only.
44	
45	## Result (run 2026-09-21, first definitions, no revision)
46	
47	300 of 300 collected, 0 failures, median 667 ms per call. `python measure.py`
48	reproduces everything below from `runs/reviewed.jsonl` with no calls.
49	
50	| test half, n = 151 | exact set | precision | recall | F1 |
51	|---|---|---|---|---|
52	| rules (`evidence-taxonomy.mjs`) | 26 (17%) | 0.63 | 0.77 | 0.69 |
53	| **Jev, t = 0.15** (chosen on tune half) | **65 (43%)** | **0.85** | 0.80 | **0.82** |
54	
55	**Pre-registered verdict: FAIL.** Precision clears 0.80 and Jev beats the rules on
56	both measures, but exact-set match is 43%, short of the 50% bar. By the rule
57	written before the run, the rules stay.
58	
59	What the number does and does not say:
60	
61	- **Jev is much better than the rules on every summary measure**: exact match 2.5×,
62	  68% fewer wrong tags (fp 52 vs 161 on the test half), F1 +0.13. The tune half
63	  (45% exact at the same t) agrees with the test half, so this is not a lucky split.
64	- **The rules' main defect is gone.** "Rehabilitation & Return to Sport" false
65	  positives drop from 68 to 1 on the test half.
66	- **Where Jev errs** (test half, fp/fn): it misses Training & Performance
67	  (23 fn) and Rehabilitation (15 fn), and over-calls Monitoring & Technology
68	  (22 fp). These are definition-boundary disagreements with the reviewers.
69	- **The 50% bar was mine**, set in the sweep without knowing how often two careful
70	  reviewers agree on an exact multi-label set. With labels of unrecorded
71	  provenance, that ceiling is unknown. The bar is not moved here after seeing
72	  the result; whether it was the right bar is Eric's call.
73	- **The tell is t = 0.15.** The best rule includes a domain when Jev gives it only a
74	  15% chance of being a *main* subject, so with the top-3 cap it has become "take the
75	  top three unless Jev is fairly sure not." The question as written ("a substantial
76	  part… a passing mention does not count") is stricter than the reviewers' habit
77	  (median 3 domains per paper). The disagreement is mostly about **how many** domains
78	  to tag, not **which** are relevant.
79	- **One definition revision is still allowed** by the pre-registration. It has not
80	  been used. Using it now would be tuned partly on test-half errors already seen,
81	  so any revision would need a fresh held-out set to count.
82	
83	## Next: the blind check (the real consumer judges, no calls)
84	
85	Jev and the rules disagree on **135 of 151** held-out papers. `evidence_tags/blind_check.md`
86	holds 20 of them (seeded), each with the paper's summary and two unlabelled tag sets,
87	A/B shuffled per paper; the key is in `runs/blind_key.json`. Eric marks A, B or =, then
88	`python evidence_tags/blind_check.py --score`.
89	
90	**Decision rule, set now:** if Jev wins **≥ 70% of Eric's non-tie picks** (14 of 20 when
91	there are no ties), replace the rules
92	for the 407 unreviewed records, tagged `taxonomySource: "jev-v1"` so they stay
93	distinguishable from reviewed labels. Below that, the rules stay and this item closes.
94	
95	## Blind check result (Eric, 2026-09-21): Jev 12, rules 8, no ties — 60%. CLOSED.
96	
97	Below the 70% bar, so **the rules stay** and nothing is written back to
98	`SportScienceResearchRepo`. Sixth item in a row measured off the map (rerank, measured the same day in `docs/RERANK_MEASUREMENT.md`, was the fifth).
99	
100	What the 20 picks show (`python evidence_tags/blind_check.py --breakdown`):
101	
102	- Jev never tagged *more* domains than the rules. Where it tagged fewer, Eric
103	  preferred Jev 10 times and the rules 6; on same-size sets it was 2–2.
104	- On **5 of the 8** papers where Eric preferred the rules, the reviewed labels were
105	  *closer to Jev*. Eric and the reviewed labels disagree often enough that "agreement
106	  with reviewed labels" was a weak yardstick — the blind check was the right gate.
107	- A preference of 60% on n = 20 is not distinguishable from a modest edge; it is
108	  nowhere near the clear win that replacing a working rule on 407 public records
109	  would need.
110	
111	**If this is ever reopened**, the one thing worth trying is not a new threshold but a
112	looser question: the reviewers and the rules both tag ~3 domains, and Jev's "main
113	subject, not a passing mention" wording is what made it stingier. That is a new
114	pre-registration on fresh held-out papers, not a revision of this one.

36	- **exact domain-set match ≥ 50% of records**, and
37	- **micro precision ≥ 0.80**,
38	
39	and beat the rules on both. Miss either and the rules stay. The rules' baseline, as
40	measured by the sweep over all 300: exact set 55/300 (18%), precision 0.63, recall
41	0.77. It is re-measured here on the same halves by running the real `.mjs`.
42	
43	**Cost ceiling.** 300 requests × ~1k tokens ≈ $0.02. Tier A: published papers only.
44	
45	## Result (run 2026-09-21, first definitions, no revision)
46	
47	300 of 300 collected, 0 failures, median 667 ms per call. `python measure.py`
48	reproduces everything below from `runs/reviewed.jsonl` with no calls.
49	
50	| test half, n = 151 | exact set | precision | recall | F1 |
51	|---|---|---|---|---|
52	| rules (`evidence-taxonomy.mjs`) | 26 (17%) | 0.63 | 0.77 | 0.69 |
53	| **Jev, t = 0.15** (chosen on tune half) | **65 (43%)** | **0.85** | 0.80 | **0.82** |
54	
55	**Pre-registered verdict: FAIL.** Precision clears 0.80 and Jev beats the rules on
56	both measures, but exact-set match is 43%, short of the 50% bar. By the rule
57	written before the run, the rules stay.
58	
59	What the number does and does not say:
60	
61	- **Jev is much better than the rules on every summary measure**: exact match 2.5×,
62	  68% fewer wrong tags (fp 52 vs 161 on the test half), F1 +0.13. The tune half
63	  (45% exact at the same t) agrees with the test half, so this is not a lucky split.
64	- **The rules' main defect is gone.** "Rehabilitation & Return to Sport" false
65	  positives drop from 68 to 1 on the test half.
66	- **Where Jev errs** (test half, fp/fn): it misses Training & Performance
67	  (23 fn) and Rehabilitation (15 fn), and over-calls Monitoring & Technology
68	  (22 fp). These are definition-boundary disagreements with the reviewers.
69	- **The 50% bar was mine**, set in the sweep without knowing how often two careful
70	  reviewers agree on an exact multi-label set. With labels of unrecorded
71	  provenance, that ceiling is unknown. The bar is not moved here after seeing
72	  the result; whether it was the right bar is Eric's call.
73	- **The tell is t = 0.15.** The best rule includes a domain when Jev gives it only a
74	  15% chance of being a *main* subject, so with the top-3 cap it has become "take the
75	  top three unless Jev is fairly sure not." The question as written ("a substantial
76	  part… a passing mention does not count") is stricter than the reviewers' habit
77	  (median 3 domains per paper). The disagreement is mostly about **how many** domains
78	  to tag, not **which** are relevant.
79	- **One definition revision is still allowed** by the pre-registration. It has not
80	  been used. Using it now would be tuned partly on test-half errors already seen,
81	  so any revision would need a fresh held-out set to count.
82	
83	## Next: the blind check (the real consumer judges, no calls)
84	
85	Jev and the rules disagree on **135 of 151** held-out papers. `evidence_tags/blind_check.md`
86	holds 20 of them (seeded), each with the paper's summary and two unlabelled tag sets,
87	A/B shuffled per paper; the key is in `runs/blind_key.json`. Eric marks A, B or =, then
88	`python evidence_tags/blind_check.py --score`.
89	
90	**Decision rule, set now:** if Jev wins **≥ 70% of Eric's non-tie picks** (14 of 20 when
91	there are no ties), replace the rules
92	for the 407 unreviewed records, tagged `taxonomySource: "jev-v1"` so they stay
93	distinguishable from reviewed labels. Below that, the rules stay and this item closes.
94	
95	## Blind check result (Eric, 2026-09-21): Jev 12, rules 8, no ties — 60%. CLOSED.
96	
97	Below the 70% bar, so **the rules stay** and nothing is written back to
98	`SportScienceResearchRepo`. Sixth item in a row measured off the map (rerank, measured the same day in `docs/RERANK_MEASUREMENT.md`, was the fifth).
99	
100	What the 20 picks show (`python evidence_tags/blind_check.py --breakdown`):
101	
102	- Jev never tagged *more* domains than the rules. Where it tagged fewer, Eric
103	  preferred Jev 10 times and the rules 6; on same-size sets it was 2–2.
104	- On **5 of the 8** papers where Eric preferred the rules, the reviewed labels were
105	  *closer to Jev*. Eric and the reviewed labels disagree often enough that "agreement
106	  with reviewed labels" was a weak yardstick — the blind check was the right gate.
107	- A preference of 60% on n = 20 is not distinguishable from a modest edge; it is
108	  nowhere near the clear win that replacing a working rule on 407 public records
109	  would need.
110	
111	**If this is ever reopened**, the one thing worth trying is not a new threshold but a
112	looser question: the reviewers and the rules both tag ~3 domains, and Jev's "main
113	subject, not a passing mention" wording is what made it stingier. That is a new
114	pre-registration on fresh held-out papers, not a revision of this one.

"""Profile what Fireflies records about who was in each meeting. Prints counts only, no names."""
import sqlite3, os, json, re
from collections import Counter
db = os.path.expanduser('~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db')
c = sqlite3.connect(db)
rows = [json.loads(d) for (d,) in c.execute("select data from transcripts")]
print('transcripts', len(rows))
keys = Counter(k for r in rows for k in r); print('keys', sorted(keys))
ME = re.compile(r'rash', re.I)
stats = Counter()
cal_types = Counter()
for r in rows:
    cal_types[r.get('calendar_type') or 'none'] += 1
    parts = [p for p in (r.get('participants') or []) if p]
    others = [p for p in parts if not ME.search(str(p))]
    att = r.get('meeting_attendees') or []
    att_others = [a for a in att if a and not ME.search(json.dumps(a))]
    spk = r.get('speakers') or []
    names = [s.get('name') if isinstance(s, dict) else s for s in spk]
    generic = [n for n in names if not n or re.match(r'^(speaker\s*\d+|unknown)$', str(n).strip(), re.I)]
    stats['has_other_participant'] += bool(others)
    stats['has_other_attendee'] += bool(att_others)
    stats['has_speakers'] += bool(names)
    stats['all_speakers_generic'] += bool(names) and len(generic) == len(names)
    stats['some_named_speaker_not_eric'] += any(n and n not in generic and not ME.search(str(n)) for n in names)
    stats['org_email_present'] += bool(r.get('organizer_email'))
    stats['any_who_signal'] += bool(others or att_others or any(n and n not in generic and not ME.search(str(n)) for n in names))
print(dict(stats))
print('calendar_type', dict(cal_types))
sample = next((r for r in rows if r.get('speakers')), None)
if sample:
    print('speaker entry shape:', {k: type(v).__name__ for k, v in (sample['speakers'][0].items() if isinstance(sample['speakers'][0], dict) else [])})

input.content:
# Fireflies: does "who was there" settle which project a meeting belongs to?

2026-09-21. The code baseline pre-registered in the leverage sweep (#4): build a Jev
meeting-to-project tagger **only if an attendee lookup settles under 80%** of
meetings. Scripts in `fireflies_probe/` print counts only, never names. Local
Fireflies cache: 279 transcripts.

## Findings

- **No attendee data exists.** `calendar_type` is empty on all 279, every meeting is
  an upload or in-person recording (no Teams/Zoom/Meet link), and only 1 meeting lists
  a participant other than Eric. There is nothing for an attendee lookup to read.
- **Speaker names are the only "who" signal**: present on 84 of 279 (30%), and on 14
  of 41 since July (34%).
- **Even named speakers rarely settle the project.** Mapping name tokens from the
  chartered projects' receivers and stakeholders (19 tokens, 4 of them on more than one
  project) to the 84 meetings that have named speakers:

  | outcome | meetings |
  |---|---|
  | points at exactly 1 project | 18 |
  | points at 2+ projects | 27 |
  | points at no chartered project | 39 |
  | no named speaker at all | 195 |

  **18 of 279 (6%) settle**, and only 18 of 84 (21%) even when every speaker is named.
  The same supervisors sit on several charters, and many meetings are with people
  who own no chartered project.

The name map is crude (capitalised tokens from charter text), so treat 6% as the right
order of magnitude, not a precise figure. It cannot plausibly reach 80%.

**Verdict: baseline FAILS to settle, so the Jev tagger passes gate 3.** The topic of
the meeting, in its summary, is the only real signal: the Choice-over-projects shape.
Not started, because Eric chose to test only #1 and #3; it is next if he wants it.

## Should Eric start naming speakers before upload?

**Not for project routing.** Perfect naming would lift settling from 6% to about 21%
of meetings, for a few minutes' work on every recording. It also puts more names into
summaries, which is exactly what the map says must be stripped before any Fireflies
text goes to an API.

Name speakers only where it pays for itself: meetings where who-said-what matters
later (commitments, action items meant for a specific person, a supervisor's
decisions). That is a judgment per meeting, not a routine.

     "Exploratory Procedure (No Significant Findings)"),
    (r"arthroscop", "Arthroscopic Procedure"),
    (r"hematoma|haematoma", "Hematoma/Infection Debridement"),
]

SURGEON_PATTERN = r"Dr\.?\s+([A-Z][A-Za-z'\-]+(?:\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z'\-]+)?)"

# Ordered, first-match-wins, applied to Section B mentions.
TAG_RULES = [
    (r"nothing surgical|non[\s-]?surgical|non[\s-]?operative(?:ly)?|no surgery"
     r"|no need (?:for|of) (?:a )?surger|isn'?t (?:absolutely )?necessary|may not gain"
     r"|not (?:an )?option|avoid(?:ed)? surger|does not need surger|do(?:es)? not need surger"
     r"|recommendation is to not (?:do )?surger|without (?:doing )?(?:a )?surger",
     "Non-Surgical / Declined / Avoided"),
    (r"status post|months? post-?op|weeks? post-?op|\d+(?:\.\d+)? (?:weeks|months) post"
     r"|post-?op (?:anterior|reconstruction|achilles|repair)|had (?:an )?orif surgery"
     r"|had surgery|surgery (?:on|in) (?:january|february|march|april|may|june|july|august"
     r"|september|october|november|december)|surgery on \d|surgical (?:follow-?up|history)"
     r"|return to play from .{0,20}(?:repair|surgery)|rehabbing from .{0,20}(?:surgery|repair)"
     r"|remove hardware|hardware removal|after surgery|since (?:his|her) surgery",
     "Additional Completed Surgery (Not in Structured Registry)"),
    (r"recommend(?:ed|s)?.{0,40}surger|surger.{0,40}recommend|would benefit from"
     r"|benefit from.{0,30}procedure|only way to correct.{0,30}surgery|will (?:need|require) surgery"
     r"|need surgery|determin(?:e|ing) if surgery|surgical intervention"
     r"|elect(?:ed)? to have.{0,20}surgery|set .{0,20}up for surgery|offered surgery"
     r"|possibility of surgery|chose to have surgery|prior to (?:his|her) .{0,15}surgery on"
     r"|second surgery|surgery (?:to|on) (?:fix|stabilize|strengthen|address|repair|expand)"
     r"|treated (?:non )?operatively or surgically|after (?:he|she) has surgery|has surgery to",
     "Surgery Discussed / Recommended / Scheduled"),
]
TAG_DEFAULT = "Review - Other / Ambiguous (verify context)"


def extract_procedure(note):
    if not isinstance(note, str) or not note.strip():
        return ""
    note_l = note.lower()
    for pattern, label in PROCEDURE_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pattern, note_l):
            return label
    return ""


def extract_surgeon(note):
    if not isinstance(note, str):
        return ""
    m = re.search(SURGEON_PATTERN, note)
    return m.group(1) if m else ""


def tag_mention(note):
    note_l = note.lower() if isinstance(note, str) else ""
    for pattern, label in TAG_RULES:
        if re.search(pattern, note_l):
            return label
    return TAG_DEFAULT


def clean_text(s):
    if not isinstance(s, str):
        return ""
    return s.replace("\n", " ").replace("\r", " ").replace("|", "/").strip()


def excerpt(note, pattern=MENTION_PATTERN, width=100):
    note = clean_text(note)
    if not note:
        return ""
    m = re.search(pattern, note, re.I)
    if not m:
        return note[:200]
    start = max(0, m.start() - width)
    end = min(len(note), m.end() + width)
    return ("..." if start > 0 else "") + note[start:end] + ("..." if end < len(note) else "")


def main():
    df = pd.read_csv(SOURCE_FILE, encoding="utf-8")
    df["Month"] = pd.to_datetime(df["DiagnosticDate"]).dt.strftime("%Y-%m")

    def classify(p):
        if isinstance(p, str) and p.strip():
            return group_pathology(p)
        return ("", "", "")

    classified = df["Pathology_Clean"].apply(classify)
    df["BodyRegion"] = classified.apply(lambda t: t[0])
    df["PathologyGroup"] = classified.apply(lambda t: t[1])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # A. Structured Surgical Registry
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    struct_mask = df["DiagnosticType"].isin(STRUCTURED_TYPES)
    a_df = df[struct_mask].copy()
    a_df["Procedure_Type"] = a_df["Note_Expanded"].apply(extract_procedure)
    a_df.loc[a_df["Procedure_Type"] == "", "Procedure_Type"] = "Not documented in note"
    a_df["Surgeon"] = a_df["Note_Expanded"].apply(extract_surgeon)
    a_df["Note_Excerpt"] = a_df["Note_Expanded"].apply(lambda n: clean_text(n)[:200])
    a_df["Mention_Tag"] = "Structured Surgical Event"
    a_out = a_df[[
        "Athlete_Clean", "Squad", "DiagnosticDate", "DiagnosticType", "Pathology_Clean",
        "BodyRegion", "PathologyGroup", "Procedure_Type", "Surgeon", "Mention_Tag", "Note_Excerpt",
    ]].copy()
    a_out["Section"] = "A - Structured Registry"
    a_out["Pathology_Clean"] = a_out["Pathology_Clean"].fillna("").str.replace(" | ", " / ", regex=False)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # B. Additional Surgery-Related Note Mentions
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    struct_athletes = set(a_df["Athlete_Clean"])
    mention_mask = df["Note_Expanded"].str.contains(MENTION_PATTERN, case=False, na=False, regex=True)
    b_df = df[mention_mask & ~df["Athlete_Clean"].isin(struct_athletes)].copy()
    b_df["Procedure_Type"] = b_df["Note_Expanded"].apply(extract_procedure)
    b_df["Surgeon"] = b_df["Note_Expanded"].apply(extract_surgeon)
    b_df["Mention_Tag"] = b_df["Note_Expanded"].apply(tag_mention)
    b_df["Note_Excerpt"] = b_df["Note_Expanded"].apply(excerpt)
    b_out = b_df[[
        "Athlete_Clean", "Squad", "DiagnosticDate", "DiagnosticType", "Pathology_Clean",
        "BodyRegion", "PathologyGroup", "Procedure_Type", "Surgeon", "Mention_Tag", "Note_Excerpt",
    ]].copy()
    b_out["Section"] = "B - Additional Note Mentions"
    b_out["Pathology_Clean"] = b_out["Pathology_Clean"].fillna("").str.replace(" | ", " / ", regex=False)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Write combined audit CSV
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    col_order = [
        "Section", "Athlete_Clean", "Squad", "DiagnosticDate", "DiagnosticType",
        "Pathology_Clean", "BodyRegion", "PathologyGroup", "Procedure_Type", "Surgeon",
        "Mention_Tag", "Note_Excerpt",
    ]
    a_out = a_out[col_order].sort_values("DiagnosticDate")
    b_out = b_out[col_order].sort_values(["Athlete_Clean", "DiagnosticDate"])
    combined = pd.concat([a_out, b_out], ignore_index=True)
    combined.to_csv(OUTPUT_CSV, index=False)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Markdown summary
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    sections = []

    header = ["# Surgery NLP Extraction — Summary", ""]
    header.append(f"Source: `{SOURCE_FILE}`  ")
    header.append(
        "Phase 2 backlog item: `Note_Expanded` surgery-related mentions are far "
        f"richer than the structured fields. Full audit trail in `{OUTPUT_CSV}` "
        f"({len(combined)} rows). Two parts:"
    )
    header.append("")
    header.append(
        "- **A. Structured Surgical Registry** — the 45 rows with `DiagnosticType` "
        "in `Surgical Procedure` / `Arthroscopic Surgery` (38 athletes). "
        "`Procedure_Type` and `Surgeon` are extracted from `Note_Expanded` via "
        "regex over the operative note."
    )
    header.append(

        "surgery/repair/reconstruction/post-op/arthroscopy pattern over "
        f"`Note_Expanded`, for the 44 athletes NOT in section A ({len(b_out)} rows). "
        "Each row is tagged via regex heuristic for staff review; several point "
        "to real surgeries with no `Surgical Procedure` row anywhere in the "
        "dataset (see B.2)."
    )
    header.append("")
    sections.append("\n".join(header))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # A.1 Registry table

    a = ["## A. Structured Surgical Registry (45 events, 38 athletes)", ""]
    a.append("### A.1 Full Registry — Chronological")
    a.append("")
    a1_df = a_out[["DiagnosticDate", "Athlete_Clean", "Squad", "BodyRegion", "PathologyGroup",
                    "Procedure_Type", "Surgeon"]].rename(

    ).reset_index(drop=True)
    a.append(md_table(a1_df))
    a.append("")

    a.append("### A.2 By Procedure Type")
    a.append("")
    proc_counts = a_out["Procedure_Type"].value_counts()
    proc_df = pd.DataFrame({"Procedure_Type": proc_counts.index, "Events": proc_counts.values})
    a.append(md_table(proc_df))
    a.append("")

    a.append("### A.3 By Month")
    a.append("")
    month_counts = a_df["Month"].value_counts().sort_index()
    month_df = pd.DataFrame({"Month": month_counts.index, "Surgeries": month_counts.values})
    a.append(md_table(month_df))
    a.append("")

    a.append("### A.4 By Body Region")
    a.append("")
    region_counts = a_out["BodyRegion"].replace("", "(non-MSK / not classified)").value_counts()
    region_df = pd.DataFrame({"BodyRegion": region_counts.index, "Surgeries": region_counts.values})
    a.append(md_table(region_df))

    a.append("### A.5 By Surgeon")

    surgeon_counts = a_out["Surgeon"].replace("", "(not identified in note)").value_counts()

    a.append(md_table(surgeon_df))
    a.append("")

    sections.append("\n".join(a))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # B. Additional mentions
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    b = [f"## B. Additional Surgery-Related Note Mentions ({len(b_out)} rows, "
         f"{b_out['Athlete_Clean'].nunique()} athletes)", ""]
    b.append(
        "Athletes NOT in the structured registry (section A), whose notes "

    )

    tag_counts = b_out["Mention_Tag"].value_counts()
    tag_df = pd.DataFrame({"Mention_Tag": tag_counts.index, "Rows": tag_counts.values})
    b.append(md_table(tag_df))
    b.append("")

    b.append("### B.2 Notable Findings — Additional Completed Surgeries")
    b.append("")
    b.append(
        "Rows tagged **Additional Completed Surgery (Not in Structured "
        "Registry)** — these describe a surgery that already happened, with no "
        "corresponding `DiagnosticType == \"Surgical Procedure\"` row anywhere in "
        "the dataset. Several have specific dates (often pre-dating the report "
        "window, June 1 2025) or identify the procedure (ACL repair, UCL repair, "
        "ankle ORIF, Achilles repair, etc.) — candidates for staff to fold into "
        "an external surgical history record."
    )
    b.append("")
    notable = b_out[b_out["Mention_Tag"] == "Additional Completed Surgery (Not in Structured Registry)"][
        ["Athlete_Clean", "Squad", "DiagnosticDate", "Pathology_Clean", "Procedure_Type", "Note_Excerpt"]
    ].rename(columns={"Athlete_Clean": "Athlete", "DiagnosticDate": "Date"}).reset_index(drop=True)
    b.append(md_table(notable))
    b.append("")

    b.append("### B.3 Full Audit Table (All Rows)")
    b.append("")
    b3_df = b_out[["Athlete_Clean", "Squad", "DiagnosticDate", "Pathology_Clean", "Mention_Tag",
                    "Procedure_Type", "Note_Excerpt"]].rename(
        columns={"Athlete_Clean": "Athlete", "DiagnosticDate": "Date"}

    b.append(md_table(b3_df))
    b.append("")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # C. Coverage summary
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    c = ["## C. Coverage Summary", ""]
    total_athletes = len(struct_athletes | set(b_out["Athlete_Clean"]))
    c_df = pd.DataFrame({
        "Group": [
            "A. Structured surgical events",

    })
    c.append(md_table(c_df))
    sections.append("\n".join(c))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Write output
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    output = "\n\n".join(sections) + "\n"
    with open(OUTPUT_MD, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:

    print(tag_counts.to_string())
    print()
    print("Total unique athletes with surgery documentation:", total_athletes)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Ath_Medicine surgery mentions — does Jev beat the regex tagger?

Item #1 of the 2026-09-21 leverage sweep. Eric cleared clinical note text for Jev on
2026-09-21 (extending Option C). Names are still stripped from the note text before
anything is sent.

## PHI handling

- Note text, the label sheet and Eric's labels live only in `notes_probe/private/`,
  which is **gitignored**. Nothing with note text is committed to this repo.
- Before any call, names are replaced in `Note_Expanded`: every token of all 534
  `Athlete_Clean` names, every staff name in `Created By` and `Prescriber`, and any
  `Dr. <Name>`. What is sent is the de-identified note only, keyed by row index.
- Committed: code, this doc, aggregate counts.

## Pre-registration (committed before any API call)

**Set.** The 60 "Section B" rows `Ath_Medicine/surgery_nlp_extraction.py` builds: notes
mentioning surgery for athletes who have no structured surgical record. Its regex tags
them 17 completed / 15 discussed / 12 declined / **16 ambiguous (27%)**. The annual
report's "17 previously undocumented completed surgeries" rests on these tags.

**Truth.** Eric labels all 60 **blind**, seeing only the de-identified note, with one of:

- **C, completed:** the note says this athlete has *already had* a surgery. This takes
  precedence: if more surgery is also discussed, it is still C.
- **P, planned:** surgery for this athlete is recommended, being considered, or
  scheduled, and none has happened yet.
- **D, declined:** surgery was considered and is not being done; treatment is
  non-surgical.
- **N, none:** the note does not describe a surgery history or decision for this
  athlete (the word is used in another sense, or refers to someone else).

**Jev.** One Choice over the same four options, with the same definitions and the same
precedence rule, plus one Noul: "has this athlete already had a surgery?" Scored on the
Choice.

**Kill test (from the sweep handoff).** Jev replaces the regex only if both hold:

1. On the **44 regex-settled** notes, Jev agrees with Eric on **≥ 90%**.
2. On the **16 regex-ambiguous** notes, Jev is correct *and* confident (top probability
   **≥ 0.60**) on **≥ 11**.

Otherwise the regex stays, with a human reading its ambiguous rows.

**Reported whatever happens:** the regex's own accuracy against Eric on the 44 settled
rows, and the completed-surgery count under Eric's labels, the regex and Jev. The 17 in
the annual report is checked either way.

**Cost.** 60 requests at under 1k tokens each, well under a cent.

## Result
